answer: One effective defense is stake-backed identity: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable deposit in a vault tied to one verified key, like a lantern that makes its history visible to peers. Creating many fake identities requires splitting capital across each one, so cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. A karst-like reputation graph adds a second price: trust flows only through completed work, so a new identity starts with no endorsements and cannot borrow another agent's standing. Forging both stake and history costs far more than one fraudulent trade gains.
